scope: Direct inspection of all eight 1280x1280 sheets (32 displayed views) and all five additional thin-case PNGs at original resolution
status: No observed implementation blocker; renderer and label-quality limitations remain

observations.finding: The selected narrow D00 region is edited; other D00 regions and the surrounding scene remain aligned. Strong blur softens the thin crack. No visible box displacement.

The overlapping D10/D20 group is edited together. Strong darkening creates a clearly visible rectangular/L-shaped intensity transition; blur weakens crack texture; noise is localized. This is a mask-realism limitation, not an unexplained coordinate change.

The D20/D10 overlap group is edited together while the separate D10 box stays unchanged. Darkening and noise have visible box-shaped boundaries; alligator structure remains visible in the displayed examples.

The selected overlapping D40/D20 pair changes together; the separate D40 instance remains unchanged. Road detail is already weak in the reference, and strong blur weakens it further. Geometry and boxes appear aligned.

The right-edge D00 box remains aligned. Its top portion is partly hidden by the 20-pixel preview title bar; the numerical annotation audit supplies the coordinate check there. Blur visibly reduces crack contrast.
The transverse crack remains visible within its D10 box. Brightness and noise boundaries are visibly rectangular; no displacement or change outside the selected neighborhood was observed.

The selected D20 annotation includes road context and part of a vehicle; the entire rectangle is affected, as specified. The other D20 box remains unchanged. D43 annotation metadata remains present. This renderer is box-group-local, not a segmentation of damage pixels.

The stored D40 annotation encloses elongated, crack-like damage. Its class is visually ambiguous from this image and should not be presented as an independently certified pothole label. The source annotation was preserved; no relabeling or exclusion was performed. Blur weakens detail but no geometric displacement is visible.

thin_case.finding: The raw crop contains transverse road damage; the selected box occupies a very small portion of the prepared road scene. Dense overlay labels obscure individual distant boxes, so the unannotated RGB views were inspected too. The roughly one-pixel-high target is difficult to resolve at 640 even before the extra shrink. A positive-area box does not establish that its fine detail remains learnable.
thin_case.decision: Retain the frozen annotation and monitor small-target behavior; do not introduce post-hoc filtering or relabeling.

numerical_preview_check: All 24 displayed candidate tiles have zero changed pixels outside the transformed selected-mask footprint plus a conservative one-pixel interpolation halo, excluding their intentional title bars. The overlays can cover pixels; this check does not replace raw-pixel verification of every candidate.
policy_context: The sheets deliberately show strongest candidate levels, not only admitted actions. All eight displayed strong-blur cases and seven of eight strong-darkening cases are rejected by their panel's routed policy. Visible artifacts can still occur for admitted noise or milder intensity edits.
limits: Only eight selected images are displayed; this is not exhaustive semantic review of all 512 images or all 13824 appearance candidates.
No annotation relabeling, exclusion, threshold adjustment or renderer change was made after viewing these results.
The retained one-pixel boundary taper does not remove rectangular appearance seams. These are a plausible training shortcut, not a measured cause of a downstream AP change.
No training or validation/test evaluation was performed by this diagnostic.
